scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Turn your phone sideways, and the screen rotates. Tilt it in a game, and the car steers. How does it feel movement?

scenes.name: mems
scenes.text: Inside is a chip with microscopic moving parts, called MEMS. Tiny silicon structures, thinner than a hair.

scenes.name: accel
scenes.text: The accelerometer has a tiny mass on springs. When the phone moves, the mass shifts, and the chip measures that shift electrically.

scenes.name: gravity
scenes.text: Gravity always pulls that mass too. So even when still, the phone knows which way is down, and rotates the screen.

scenes.name: gyro
scenes.text: A gyroscope has a part that vibrates. When you twist the phone, that vibration gets pushed sideways, revealing how fast you're rotating.

scenes.name: uses
scenes.text: Together they count your steps, steer games, steady your camera, and help maps know which way you're facing.

scenes.name: compass
scenes.text: Many phones also have a magnetometer, a digital compass that senses Earth's magnetic field.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Mass, springs, vibration, compass. Your phone feels every move. Follow for more on how things really work.
